classification.classification_note: The saved sanitizer trace reports a READ of size 4 from freed heap memory in xmlStaticCopyNode after xmlXIncludeLoadTxt reuses a cached xmlNodePtr that xmlreader.c had already freed.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in XInclude processing: xmlXIncludeLoadTxt (xinclude.c) can end up calling xmlStaticCopyNode (tree.c) on a node that has already been freed (by the XML reader code), resulting in a read of freed heap memory. An attacker-controlled XML with XInclude can trigger this, causing crashes, memory corruption, or potentially enabling information disclosure or further exploitation.
bug_description.original_source: sample metadata issue_description and staged sanitizer_trace.txt
bug_description.normalized: The saved PoC drives libxml2's xml fuzz target through XML Reader based XInclude processing. xmlTextReaderRead() reaches an xi:include element, expands it, and calls xmlXIncludeProcessNode(). In xmlXIncludeLoadTxt(), the first inclusion of a text resource allocates an xml text node with xmlNewText(NULL), fills node->content from the external text stream, and caches that xmlNodePtr in ctxt->txtTab via xmlXIncludeAddTxt(ctxt, node, URL). Control then returns to xmlTextReaderRead(), whose normal cleanup path unlinks and frees old reader-owned nodes with xmlTextReaderFreeNode() when reader->preserves == 0, reader->in_xinclude == 0, reader->entNr == 0, and the previous node is not preserved. The saved ASan free stack shows that cleanup frees the same text node allocation created in xmlXIncludeLoadTxt(). On a later include of the same URL, xmlXIncludeLoadTxt() hits the duplicate-URL cache path, reloads the dangling pointer from ctxt->txtTab[i], and calls xmlCopyNode(ctxt->txtTab[i], 1). xmlCopyNode dispatches to xmlStaticCopyNode(), which immediately reads node->type from the freed xmlNode object, producing the recorded heap-use-after-free at tree.c:4197. The patch fixes the bug by changing txtTab from xmlNodePtr storage to duplicated xmlChar * text content and recreating a fresh node with xmlNewText(ctxt->txtTab[i]) instead of copying a stale cached node object.

source.description: First project statement that materializes attacker-controlled included text as the xmlNode object later cached in ctxt->txtTab and eventually reused after reader cleanup.
source.value_from: sanitizer_trace.txt records the allocation site for the freed object as xmlNewText at src/tree.c:2447, called from src/xinclude.c:1897 inside xmlXIncludeLoadTxt. The same function then fills that node from the attacker-controlled external text resource before caching it for duplicate URL reuse.

sink.description: Unsafe dereference of the stale cached xmlNodePtr. The recorded crash is a read of the freed node header when xmlCopyNode dispatches into xmlStaticCopyNode().

root_cause.description: The XInclude cache stores the reader-owned xmlNodePtr itself instead of duplicating stable text content or transferring ownership, so ctxt->txtTab retains a pointer that can become dangling after xmlreader cleanup frees the node.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later dangling pointer originates from this text node allocation, which the saved ASan trace also names as the original heap allocation before reader cleanup frees it.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific format admission gate: the parsed XML must produce an element in the XInclude namespace so the reader enters XInclude processing instead of ordinary element traversal.

fine_trace.note: xmlXIncludeLoadTxt creates an xml text node that will hold attacker-controlled included text. The saved ASan allocation stack identifies this allocation as the object later freed and reused.
Root cause. The XInclude cache saves the xmlNodePtr itself in ctxt->txtTab, preserving only an alias to reader-managed node storage rather than a durable copy of the text payload.

After XInclude processing returns, the reader cleanup path frees a previously traversed node when it is not preserved and reader->in_xinclude == 0. The saved ASan free stack records xmlTextReaderRead at this line calling into xmlTextReaderFreeNodeList to free the same text-node allocation from step 1.
A later include of the same URL takes the duplicate-resource reuse path, selecting the cached entry instead of reloading the text resource.
The duplicate-URL branch reloads the stale pointer from ctxt->txtTab[i] and passes it to xmlCopyNode as if it still referenced a live xmlNode object.
xmlCopyNode forwards the cached pointer into xmlStaticCopyNode. The pointer is non-NULL even though the underlying allocation was freed, so execution continues into field access instead of stopping.
Sink. xmlStaticCopyNode reads the node header from freed heap memory to dispatch on node->type, matching the saved ASan heap-use-after-free read at this exact line.

allocation_context.note: sanitizer_trace.txt records the original allocation as xmlNewText at src/tree.c:2447 called from xmlXIncludeLoadTxt at src/xinclude.c:1897.

free_context.note: sanitizer_trace.txt records the free stack as xmlTextReaderRead -> xmlTextReaderFreeNode -> xmlTextReaderFreeNodeList, with the xmlTextReaderRead frame at src/xmlreader.c:1504.

sanitizer_ground_truth.reproduction_rate: 1/1 recorded Stage 01 run reproduced on the vulnerable commit; the same PoC was recorded clean on the fixed commit.

poc.trigger: The witness is an XML document processed by the libxml2 xml fuzz target that contains XInclude text processing and repeats the same included text URL so xmlXIncludeLoadTxt first caches a text node for that URL and later revisits the duplicate-URL cache path after reader cleanup has freed the cached node object.

format.name: XML with repeated XInclude text reference
format.contract: The input must parse as XML, reach an element in the XInclude namespace, and cause at least two xmlXIncludeLoadTxt calls for the same resolved text URL so the second call executes the xmlStrEqual(URL, ctxt->txturlTab[i]) cache-hit branch after the original cached text node has been freed by xmlTextReaderRead cleanup.
